title: QBR Deck Starter Kits — Standard + Enterprise
content:
Purpose: quick-to-run QBR slide sets for (A) Standard customers and (B) Enterprise customers. Two parallel tracks share core slides; enterprise variation has expanded security, roadmap, and renewal choreography slides.

Usage notes (short):
- Use Standard kit for customers on < $X monthly spend / self-serve accounts. Keep to 30 minutes.
- Use Enterprise kit for named accounts, multi-stakeholder reviews, and accounts in renewal window. Plan 45–60 minutes.
- Bring: metrics export (tokens, latency, errors), deployment config, open action tracker, renewal timeline.

=== Slide-by-slide outline (common core) ===
1) Title + Meeting Logistics
   - Title: QBR — [Customer name] 
   - Date, host (AM/PM timezone), attendees (roles)
   - Purpose: align on health, goals, risks, and next steps
   - Speaker note: confirm timebox and ask if any additional topics to add

2) Executive TL;DR (1 slide)
   - Short bullets: Current health (green/amber/red), adoption trend (↑/↓/%), renewal posture (on track/at-risk), 2 recommended asks (e.g., pilot expansion, contract re-up)
   - Speaker note: state the single-slide summary up-front for execs

3) Business outcomes & customer goals (1–2 slides)
   - Customer stated goals from kickoff / last QBR
   - Progress notes (what changed)
   - Open question: are these still top priority?

4) Usage & efficiency metrics (2–3 slides)
   - Key metrics: total tokens, API calls by product, P95 latency, error rate, cost per 1k tokens (approx), embeddings volume
   - Visual cue hints: show trend (30/90 day) and highlight anomalies
   - Speaker note: call out whether changes are due to product usage, release, or config changes (caching, batch size)

5) Quality & correctness signals (1–2 slides)
   - Uptime and incident summary (last 90d)
   - Notable regressions or model quality issues tied to prompt/evals
   - Recent evals / scorecard highlights (precision/recall or business metric proxy)

6) Savings & cost optimization (1 slide)
   - Current spend vs forecast (30/90 day)
   - Suggested levers: batching, KV caching, quantized model variant, route to Dedicated if long tail cost high
   - Quick calc: estimated monthly savings if apply X lever (guesstimate)

7) Roadmap & integration items (1 slide)
   - Upcoming product features (console, rollout, metrics) relevant to customer
   - Integration blockers or requests (SAML, VPC peering, custom KMS)

8) Risks & mitigation (1 slide)
   - Top 3 risks (e.g., renewal budget timing, data residency, performance SLOs) and proposed mitigations

9) Ask / CTA / Renewal summary (1 slide)
   - Renewal window and contract anchor (dates)
   - Desired outcome from this QBR (extend pilot, exec intro, contract renewal)
   - Next steps owners + dates (owner initials + due date)

10) Appendix (as-needed)
   - Expanded metric charts, raw tables, incident timelines, eval prompt sets

=== Enterprise variation (adds / expands slides) ===
A) Stakeholder map (1 slide)
   - Decision makers, technical approvers, procurement contacts, legal/security reviewer (names + roles + readiness)
   - Speaker note: confirm escalation path prior to renewal

B) Security & compliance deep-dive (2 slides)
   - Data flow diagram (textual summary), KMS/HSM posture, SOC/ISO artifacts available, privacy controls in place
   - List of outstanding items for compliance signoff (e.g., on-prem connector, audit log retention)

C) SLA & performance commitments (1 slide)
   - Current 90-day SLO performance vs SLA target
   - Proposed Dedicated or private deployment options with throughput/latency numbers and estimated cost delta

D) Commercial & renewal choreography (1–2 slides)
   - Renewal timeline visual (90 / 60 / 30 / 14 / 7 days) with tasks per milestone (procurement, legal, SOW); owners
   - Contingency plan if procurement misses date (temporary pricing hold, executive cutover)

E) Custom roadmap & co-investment asks (1 slide)
   - Requested features and Redwood ask (engineering time, POC funding)
   - Proposed success criteria and pilot definition

=== Playbook fragments (copyable text snippets) ===
Pre-QBR checklist (owner: CSM):
- Export usage: yesterday, 30d, 90d (tokens, calls, errors)
- Export latency percentiles and batch config for main endpoints
- Run eval set used for last release; capture failure examples
- Confirm attendees and share agenda 3 days prior
- Prepare 1-slide exec TL;DR and one appendix chart for any anomaly

Renewal risk scoring (quick heuristic):
- Score 1–10 across: spend trend, engagement (DAU/MAU or API callers), exec sponsorship, integration blockers, support incidents
- 1–3 = low risk, 4–6 = medium, 7–10 = high risk
- If score >=7: escalate to AE + Solutions Eng + Solutions Architect meeting within 7 days

Immediate remediation play (for high-risk enterprise accounts):
- 48-hour triage: CSM + SRE + Solutions Eng to reproduce perf issue or security ask
- If cost concern: run "Cost Quick Audit" (2–3 config checks: caching, batch size, model-family) and propose top-2 quick wins
- Schedule executive sync (10–15 minutes) to cover commercial implications and mitigation plan

Sample renewal tracker (single-slide text table for insertion):
- Customer | Renewal date | Current ARR | Renewal Rep | Risk score | Key blocker | Next checkpoint
- Example: Acme Corp | 2026-05-15 | $120k | Jordan A. | 6 | Procurement timeline | 2026-04-01

Slide tips & speaker notes (practical):
- Keep visuals simple: 3 bullets per slide max for execs
- Use color only to flag risk (green/amber/red). Avoid heavy charts unless asked
- Bring 1–2 action items to the end of every slide — don’t leave open threads
- For enterprise meetings, pre-send a 1-page exec TL;DR to procurement or exec sponsor 48 hours prior

Versioning & template housekeeping:
- Filename pattern: qbr-<standard|enterprise>-<YYYYMM>-v<number>.pptx
- Track changes in GitHub PR and link in the Confluence canonical playbook
- Notes to self: add a ‘customer wins’ slide template with short quotes / metrics next round

Open questions / things to iterate in this draft:
- Do we want a templated slide for "Model drift / rollback history" for ML-heavy customers? (pros: shows rigor, cons: may raise alarm)
- Should the enterprise kit include a pre-built legal checklist or just pointers to legal templates?
- Add a lightweight one-page summary specifically for procurement teams?

Quick links for CSMs (copy into slide footer or appendix):
- Metrics export step: https://internal-redwood/tools/metrics-export
- Standard QBR playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/QBR+Playbook+Canonical
- Renewal checklist (spreadsheet): https://sheets.redwood.ai/s/renewal-tracker

-- end of starter kit --

Author note: This is intentionally concise so CSMs can copy/paste into slide master. Will iterate based on PM feedback and AE/solutions needs.
